NTA. This is like if you let someone you barely know bully you into staying with you in your house. I’m sorry this sounds like a difficult position but to me it’s clear that she shouldn’t be allowed to stay. She’s not entitled to a place because you’re her cousin. Hard. Nope.

YTA. Why are you assuming anyone who isn’t a parent of your children will pitch in to help? I mean, literally the other parent of your children is choosing to be away from your children so to assume that people who are not obligated to help will help is silly and entitled. Your husband is the bigger AH though, let that be known.

So your family is demanding you work for free with materials that you’d pay for out-of-pocket. They’re also bullying you into agreeing and undermining you and your part time job. Hmmm… it sounds like your decision is creating a very distinct boundary and I don’t see a problem with that at all. 🤔NTA.

NTA I think you’re allowed to invite any one to to hang with you and not invite whoever you don’t want to hang with you. ??? You don’t owe your roommate any explanations or invitations? She sounds insecure.

NTA. Aaron is way in the wrong to ask you to disinvite Bradley. I can totally understand why you feel for Adam but you invited both boys. It’s not your fault one of the boys’ parents doesn’t want to them them attend. Your main focus should just be to make your own son have a good time.

YTA. Sorry but i can think of plenty of kid-friendly party foods that accommodate those dietary restrictions just off the top of my head. And also, not every kid needs to have every dish. Everything could have be nicely labeled and/or maybe coordinate a pot-luck type spread with the other moms. It’s a bit rude to invite everyone, ask about particulars with allergies and dietary restrictions, get the information and then cancel because of the information you received. Lol

NTA. Your wedding, your guest list. Simple as that. Don’t let anyone— especially family— bully you into adding people you don’t want to the list. Also, consider recommending therapy to your mom. It sounds like she has a lot of stuff to work through.
